title: Which Growth Stocks Are Actually Cheap?
creator: Couch Investor
summary: On Varun's 'Investing Moats' channel, guest Neil (Couch Investor) ranks 11 stocks across tiers from 'screaming buy' to 'wait'/'avoid'. His verdicts: SOFI screaming buy (DCF-implied ~$24-25; fast-growing, increasingly profitable fintech, though the tech platform disappointed); GOOGL buy (still a buy despite doubling; search/ads/Cloud/TPU/YouTube juggernaut); RDDT buy (bought at $174.75; fast-growing, profitable, AI data-licensing optionality); META screaming buy (2022-like sentiment, core business firing, PE under 20); UBER buy (AV distribution layer, ~20 AV partnerships, delivery growth); PLTR buy (bought at $107, now $117; down ~50% from $200, business accelerating, PEG ~1); MELI screaming buy (~$1,600-1,700; 29 straight quarters of 30%+ revenue growth); AMD wait (~$500s; MI400 ramp coming but priced in - buy a big dip); NBIS wait at $240 (loves the business, wants it lower); ADBE wait (cheap and growing but zero momentum, disruption risk); MU wait (not buying more here despite loving the business - better opportunities elsewhere); PYPL avoid ('cannot trust them anymore'). Host Varun is more conservative throughout (SoFi only a 'wait' for him, Adobe a personal avoid, Palantir a 'wait' hoping for $70-80) and agrees Meta is a screaming buy. Note: tier labels garbled ('weight' = wait, 'void' = avoid-ish); Varun's SoFi line is ambiguous and treated as host-only wait.
